question:
A data-analysis class arranges three sets of observations as the columns of $A=\begin{bmatrix}1 & 2 & 3\\2 & 5 & 8\\3 & 7 & 11\end{bmatrix}$. The students notice that one column may be expressible using the other two. To test the effect of a small data correction, they form $B$ by changing only the entry $11$ in $A$ to $12$. They then compare the determinants to decide whether the original and corrected column sets are dependent.

(a) Establish the relation among the columns of $A$.

(b) Use this relation to determine $|A|$.

(c) Evaluate $|B|$ after the correction.

(d) Interpret what the determinant values indicate about the column sets of $A$ and $B$.
explanation:
(a)
The columns of $A$ are
$$C_1=\begin{bmatrix}1\\2\\3\end{bmatrix},\quad C_2=\begin{bmatrix}2\\5\\7\end{bmatrix},\quad C_3=\begin{bmatrix}3\\8\\11\end{bmatrix}$$
Now,
$$2C_2-C_1=2\begin{bmatrix}2\\5\\7\end{bmatrix}-\begin{bmatrix}1\\2\\3\end{bmatrix}=\begin{bmatrix}3\\8\\11\end{bmatrix}=C_3$$
Therefore,
$$C_3=2C_2-C_1$$

(b)
Since one column is a linear combination of the other two columns, the columns are dependent. Therefore,
$$|A|=0$$

(c)
The corrected matrix is
$$B=\begin{bmatrix}1 & 2 & 3\\2 & 5 & 8\\3 & 7 & 12\end{bmatrix}$$
Expanding along the first row,
$$|B|=1\begin{vmatrix}5 & 8\\7 & 12\end{vmatrix}-2\begin{vmatrix}2 & 8\\3 & 12\end{vmatrix}+3\begin{vmatrix}2 & 5\\3 & 7\end{vmatrix}$$
$$|B|=(60-56)-2(24-24)+3(14-15)$$
$$|B|=4-0-3=1$$

(d)
For $A$, the determinant is zero, so its columns are dependent and $A$ is singular. For $B$,
$$|B|=1\neq0$$
Therefore, the corrected columns are independent and $B$ is non-singular. Changing one entry has removed the dependence among the columns.

options.D:
(a) $C_3=2C_2-C_1$
(b) $|A|=0$
(c) $|B|=1$
(d) The columns of $A$ are dependent and $A$ is singular, while the columns of $B$ are independent and $B$ is non-singular
